newsitem.title: USA: NYS Gov expects to sign bill for NYC's new agency.
newsitem.headline: NYS Gov expects to sign bill for NYC's new agency.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki said Wednesday he expected to sign a bill creating a new financing arm for New York City, which the legislature approved earlier, although he gave no date.

"I expect I will, yes. I will obviously read it when it passes, but I expect I will," Pataki told reporters in Albany at a news conference he held to introduce a new bill on reforming the criminal justice system.
The new agency, which will be called the New York City Transitional Finance Authority, is expected to start selling debt early in the city's 1998 fiscal year, which starts on July 1.
The Authority will be allowed to issue as much as $7.5 billion of bonds that will be backed by the city's personal income taxes over the next four years.

Developed to help the city get around its state-imposed debt cap, the Authority will sunset once a constitutional amendment is approved that will change the method used to calculate New York City's debt cap, which now is based on a five-year average of real estate prices.

The built-in delay in the present method has sharply reduced how much general obligation debt the city is authorized to sell, and it was expected to hit its limit about one month before the end of its 1997 fiscal year.
